note: MOVER LIGHT FIELDS, PROVED LIVE (opening-set retrofit phase 1, doc 36 Q116). The audit found the one lighting fault every room shares: the renderer breathes a lamp's pool over the PLATE and never over the people, so Thad crossed the saloon's orange pool in a cool blue coat. A lamp may now declare `movers` {strength, colour, reach, radius, strengthByState}; a mover whose feet stand in the field is flat-tinted toward the colour by strength x square falloff (engine/render/LightFields.ts; unit tests tests/light-fields.test.ts). A lamp that declares nothing touches nobody, so a room that declares none is unchanged to the pixel. Measured here: each capture's drawn Thad against his own source frame scaled to the drawn bounds, over opaque pixels only, so the shift is the tint and not the plate.
reading: Main Street: in the saloon pool the figure shifts +26 red / -19 blue against its source frame (mean abs 46); out of the pool 14 (a walk frame's nearest-neighbour rescale accounts for the residual; the field's own contribution there computes to 0.01); under the office lantern the shift is +5 red at a point 43 px outside its 200 px reach-scaled radius. The Nugget: by the stove +7 red (field weight 0.037 at 154 px of 260); away from every field and at the bar end (outside bar_lamps' reach) the figure is drawn to within 2.1 of its source, which is the untouched case: a mover the field does not reach is not touched. PROPORTIONAL AND DETERMINISTIC, as the unit tests state and the live run shows; whether the strengths are RIGHT is Tyler's eye on the review sheets, and the numbers are per room in the annotation, not in code.
unchangedWhereUndeclared: Room 1 and Room 5 declare no `movers` on any lamp. Room 5's shipping proof (renders/proofs/assay-office-shipping/) ran after the renderer change with no candidates and passed; Room 1's regression is in the phase-1 test list.
